precepts.text: As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers. Take the young men in regular clothes six months in the truth: they are going to follow the example of the officers that have been here eight, nine, ten years. If you are bashful, afraid, timid, and shy, your spirit is telling those brothers it is okay to be like this. It shall not be so in here.
precepts.point: This is the king. If the king is scared, what is that going to do to the men under him? If the officer is fearful, it spreads to the soldiers under him.
precepts.why:
“And when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.” He was scared. This is the king. If the king is scared, what is that going to do to the men under him? If the officer is fearful, what is that going to do to the soldiers under him? It is going to spread.

“As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers”: so are they that are under him. “And what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein.” Whatever man the ruler is, like King Saul, such are all that dwell under him.

Take an example. Some brothers have been here six months, a year maybe, not long, still in regular clothes. Some officers have been here eight, nine, ten years. Those young men in the regular shirts are going to follow the example of the officers in the purple shirts. So if you are bashful, afraid, timid and shy, what does that communicate to them spiritually? That they can be timid, shy, fearful and bashful too. You don’t have to say nothing; your spirit is telling them, it’s okay to be like this, the officer can be fearful and timid, so I’ll follow his example, now I know how to move around in here.

It shall not be so. It shall not be so in here.

precepts.text: For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth. A soldier broke it down: you trick yourself into being scared because you make up things in your mind which are not really there. And you also have a lack of faith: your faith is supposed to be in the Lord, but a lot of the time your faith is only in what you can see with your eyes.
precepts.point: This is the king. If the king is scared, what is that going to do to the men under him? If the officer is fearful, it spreads to the soldiers under him.
precepts.why:
Saul saw the host of the Philistines and “was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.” What is fear? “For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth.”

A soldier broke it down: the succours go into comfort, and fear betrays that comfort. What reason offers is the lies you make up in your head. You trick yourself into being scared, because you make up things in your mind which ain’t really there.

And on top of that, fear is a lack of faith. Your faith is supposed to be in the Lord, but a lot of the time your faith is basically what you can see with your eyes. Saul looked at the host of the Philistines with his eyes and his heart trembled, instead of trusting the Lord who had made him king.

precepts.text: For we walk by faith, not by sight. We fear what we physically see, but we do not fear breaking God's commandments. That we should fear.
precepts.point: This is the king. If the king is scared, what is that going to do to the men under him? If the officer is fearful, it spreads to the soldiers under him.
precepts.why:
“For we walk by faith, not by sight.” Christians use that all the time and don’t know what it means. But in this aspect we can use it about fear.

We fear what we see. We don’t fear the Lord; we fear what we physically see. A brother at camp gets unruly with us, he’s got a gun or a knife or whatever, and we fear that. But we don’t fear breaking God’s commandments. That we don’t really fear.

That was Saul. When he “saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid.” He walked by sight. He feared the Philistines he could see and the people who were scattering from him, but he did not fear transgressing the commandment of the Lord, and it cost him the kingdom.

precepts.text: For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind. The Lord never gave us that spirit. Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, but be thou partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God.
precepts.point: This is the king. If the king is scared, what is that going to do to the men under him? If the officer is fearful, it spreads to the soldiers under him.
precepts.why:
“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear.” The Bible says the Lord never gave us that spirit. So the fear Saul had when his heart greatly trembled goes back into a lack of faith.

“But of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” We are supposed to have the spirit of power, love and a sound mind.

“Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but be thou partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God.” We are not supposed to be ashamed of the testimony of Christ. The bashful brother is ashamed and afraid; the one who has God’s spirit partakes of the afflictions of the gospel by the power of God.

precepts.text: And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell. This is the level we have to get to: fear the Most High, not man.
precepts.point: This is the king. If the king is scared, what is that going to do to the men under him? If the officer is fearful, it spreads to the soldiers under him.
precepts.why:
“And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul.” This is the level we have to get to: where we are not afraid of those brothers and sisters, and the other nations, that can kill the body and have power over us in this society.

“But rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.” That is the Lord. We need to fear the Lord, the one who can kill body and soul in hell.

Saul feared the Philistines and feared the people, and not the Lord. So, back to 1 Samuel 28:6: “when Saul enquired of the Lord, the Lord answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.” The Lord was not dealing with Saul anymore. He went to the witch at Endor, the same kind he had put out of the land, and Samuel told him, “the Lord is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy.” Because he was bashful, self-willed, easily manipulated and made excuses, he lost the kingdom. Fear the Most High, not man.

precepts.text: There shall not be found among you any one that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits. This is the commandment Saul turned around and broke.
precepts.point: And Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment, and came to the woman by night. And the woman said, Behold, thou knowest what Saul hath done: wherefore then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die?
precepts.why:
This is the commandment Saul turned around and broke: “There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits.” The Lord said none of these would be found among Israel.

Saul had just rid the land of all of them: the soothsayers, the witches, the familiar spirits and the wizards. That is what the woman at En-dor throws back at him: “thou knowest what Saul hath done, how he hath cut off those that have familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land: wherefore then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die?” You trying to get me killed.

Now the Lord has stopped answering him, “neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets”, and the same man who cut them off says, “Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and enquire of her.” Find me a wizard so I can know what is going on. His mind is all over the place. He is double-minded, breaking the very commandment he had enforced, and he disguises himself and goes by night so no one will see it.

That is where bashfulness leads: self-willed, disobedient, deceitful, making excuses, easily manipulated. Samuel tells him the Lord “is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy.” The Lord rent the kingdom out of his hand and gave it to David, and Saul and his sons would be with Samuel the next day. “There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness.” Saul never believed in himself, so he never believed God; he had Samuel's counsel the whole time and would not listen, and when that guidance was gone he ran to the very thing the law forbade.

precepts.text: This is the law concerning Amalek that Samuel was referencing: Israel was commanded to blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven, and Saul did not do it.
precepts.point: The reason is stated plainly: because Saul obeyed not the voice of the Lord, nor executed his fierce wrath upon Amalek. The Most High gave a law concerning Amalek, and Saul did not carry it out; that history was read earlier in this book.

note.label: 1 Samuel 28: Saul and the Woman with the Familiar Spirit

precepts.why:
“Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt; How he met thee by the way, and smote the hindmost of thee, even all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary; and he feared not God.” So Israel was commanded, “thou shalt blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven; thou shalt not forget it.”

This is the law concerning Amalek that Samuel was referencing, and Saul did not do it. Samuel said it plainly: “Because thou obeyedst not the voice of the Lord, nor executedst his fierce wrath upon Amalek, therefore hath the Lord done this thing unto thee this day.” That history was read earlier in this book.

So the Lord “is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy”, and he did to Saul exactly as he spake by Samuel: “the Lord hath rent the kingdom out of thine hand, and given it to thy neighbour, even to David.”

precepts.text: Samuel's prophecy from the grave, fulfilled to the letter on mount Gilboa: Saul and his sons died the next day, and Israel was delivered into the hand of the Philistines.
precepts.point: Remember what we read in chapter 28: when Saul went and conjured up the spirit of Samuel, Samuel said to him, To morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me. He prophesied unto Saul what was going to happen, and now we read the fulfillment of that prophecy.
precepts.why:
Remember what we read in chapter 28. When Saul went and conjured up the spirit of Samuel, Samuel said to him, “to morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me: the Lord also shall deliver the host of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.” He prophesied unto Saul what was going to happen, and now we read the fulfillment of that prophecy, to the letter.

Saul said to his armourbearer, “Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through, and abuse me.” What Saul was fearful of is what you see in war, how men will abuse their captives, killing them and abusing their bodies. He was already wounded and could not get away, so instead of being taken captive he told his armourbearer to kill him.

“But his armourbearer would not; for he was sore afraid. Therefore Saul took a sword, and fell upon it.” His armourbearer “fell likewise upon his sword, and died with him. So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armourbearer, and all his men, that same day together.” Saul and his sons died the next day, and Israel was delivered into the hand of the Philistines, as Samuel said.

precepts.text: Saul sought out a woman with a familiar spirit at Endor and disguised himself to go to her by night.
precepts.point: The last straw for Saul was seeking that familiar spirit. Through Samuel the Most High told him he would join him the next day. The difference is that Samuel died righteously.
precepts.why:
Here is the very thing Chronicles speaks of. Saul told his servants, “Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and enquire of her.” They found one at Endor, and “Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment,” and came to her by night with two men.

He asked her, “divine unto me by the familiar spirit, and bring me him up, whom I shall name unto thee.” The one he wanted brought up was Samuel. This is Saul “asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit, to enquire of it”, the last straw that cost him his life and his kingdom.

precepts.text: Saul was afraid of the Philistine host and inquired of the Most High, who answered him not by dreams, Urim, or prophets, so he turned to the witch.
precepts.point: The last straw for Saul was seeking that familiar spirit. Through Samuel the Most High told him he would join him the next day. The difference is that Samuel died righteously.
precepts.why:
This is what drove Saul to the witch. “And when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.” He enquired of the Most High, “the Lord answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.”

So Saul turned to the witch instead. Rather than inquiring of the Most High, he went to the left hand, and that is why Chronicles records that he “enquired not of the Lord: therefore he slew him”.

precepts.text: The woman brought up Samuel, an old man covered with a mantle, and Saul bowed himself to the ground before the word she carried.
precepts.point: The last straw for Saul was seeking that familiar spirit. Through Samuel the Most High told him he would join him the next day. The difference is that Samuel died righteously.
precepts.why:
The woman brought up Samuel. “And when the woman saw Samuel, she cried with a loud voice”, and she knew then who had come to her: “Why hast thou deceived me? for thou art Saul.” She said, “I saw gods ascending out of the earth”, and “An old man cometh up; and he is covered with a mantle.” Saul “perceived that it was Samuel, and he stooped with his face to the ground, and bowed himself.”

Through Samuel the Most High told Saul he would join him the next day. Both men died, but the difference is that Samuel died righteously. Saul died for his transgression, for not keeping the word of the Lord, and for seeking that familiar spirit.

points: Samuel was dead, and Saul had put away those that had familiar spirits and the wizards out of the land. The Philistines gathered themselves together, and when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.
And when Saul enquired of the Lord, the Lord answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets. The Lord was not dealing with Saul anymore.

Then said Saul unto his servants, Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit. Saul just rid the land of all the soothsayers, the familiar spirits, and the wizards; now he says find me one so I can know what is going on. His mind is all over the place; he is double-minded.

And Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment, and came to the woman by night. And the woman said, Behold, thou knowest what Saul hath done: wherefore then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die?

Then said Samuel, Wherefore then dost thou ask of me, seeing the Lord is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy? Imagine that: the Lord is your enemy now, Saul. Because you were bashful, you were self-willed, you broke the commandments of the Lord, you were deceitful, you lied, you made excuses, you were easily manipulated. It all went back to Saul being bashful.
The Lord hath rent the kingdom out of thine hand, and given it to thy neighbour, even to David: because thou obeyedst not the voice of the Lord, nor executedst his fierce wrath upon Amalek.

Moreover the Lord will also deliver Israel with thee into the hand of the Philistines: and to morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me. Your day is over, Saul: no more kingdom, no more life. Cut off.
What Saul was doing when he went to the woman with the familiar spirit is called necromancy. Look that word up: it is when you go to somebody that conjures up spirits.
Saul turned to this because the Lord was departed from him and answered him no more, neither by prophets nor by dreams, so he had Samuel conjured up to tell him what to do.

note.label: 1 Samuel 28: Saul and the Woman with the Familiar Spirit

points: Samuel asks Saul why he inquires of him, seeing the Lord is departed from him and is become his enemy. The Lord did to Saul exactly as he spake by Samuel: he rent the kingdom out of Saul's hand and gave it to his neighbour, even to David.

note.label: 1 Samuel 28: Saul and the Woman with the Familiar Spirit

points: The reason is stated plainly: because Saul obeyed not the voice of the Lord, nor executed his fierce wrath upon Amalek. The Most High gave a law concerning Amalek, and Saul did not carry it out; that history was read earlier in this book.

note.label: 1 Samuel 28: Saul and the Woman with the Familiar Spirit

points: Tomorrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me means tomorrow you and your sons are going to die; you are going to be with me. Samuel prophesied from his grave, and he also declared that the Lord would deliver the host of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.

note.label: 1 Samuel 28: Saul and the Woman with the Familiar Spirit

points: Saul fell straightway all along the earth, sore afraid because of the words of Samuel, and there was no strength in him, for he had eaten no bread all the day nor all the night.

The chapter in sum: Saul inquired of the Lord and was not answered, so he turned to a woman with a familiar spirit and conjured up Samuel. Samuel told him that because of his disobedience the Lord was not dealing with him anymore, and prophesied that tomorrow Saul and his sons would be with him.

note.label: 1 Samuel 28: Saul and the Woman with the Familiar Spirit

points: The woman reminded Saul that she had put her life in her hand and obeyed his voice, and asked him to let her set a morsel of bread before him that he might have strength for his way. He refused at first, but his servants together with the woman compelled him; she killed the fat calf, baked unleavened bread, and they did eat and went away that night.
